blocks.source: Benedicti sint sancti Joachim et Anna, ex quibus benedicta Virgo Maria sine originali labe concepta et nata est.
blocks.english: Blessed be Saints Joachim and Anne, of whom the Blessed Virgin Mary was conceived without original stain and born.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, labia mea aperies.

blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus, in adjutorium meum intende.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine, ad adjuvandum me festina.

blocks.source: A Septuagesima usque ad Pascha, loco Alleluia, dicitur: Laus tibi, Domine, Rex aeternae gloriae.
blocks.english: From Septuagesima until Easter, instead of Alleluia, the following is said: Praise to Thee, O Lord, King of everlasting glory.
blocks.editorialNote: The season begins at Septuagesima, before Lent. Prepared English corrects the reused Lent rubric; original English and provenance are retained.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: During Lent until Easter, instead of the alleluia the following is said: Praise to Thee, O Lord, King of everlasting glory.

blocks.source: O bina conjugalis Exempla foederis! O Joachim, qualis Mariae conjugis! O Anna, quem nepotem, Quam nacta filiam! O Joachim, dotem Quis optet alteram!
blocks.english: O two examples of the marriage covenant! O Joachim, what a husband thou art to thy wife! O Anne, what a grandson, what a daughter thou hast obtained! O Joachim, who would desire another dowry!

blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Deus, qui prae omnibus Sanctis tuis beatos Joachim et Annam genitrices Filii tui parentes esse voluisti: concede, quaesumus; ut quos devoto cultu veneramur in terris, eorum quoque patrocinia sentiamus in caelis. Per eundem Dominum nostrum.

blocks.source: Oratio ad S. Joachim.
blocks.english: Prayer to Saint Joachim.

blocks.source: O sancte Joachim, cui nomen esse est inditum, quod praeparationem Domini significat. Tu enim ad vivum Dei templum praeparandum a Deo electus es, in quo Filio ejus Unigenito habitare placuit. O beatissime Pater, a quo suscepta est illa filia, quae in Dei Matrem, ac coeli terraeque Reginam est assumpta! O quanto illum amore et reverentia excepisti! qua cura et sollicitudine enutrivisti! quam praeclaro humilitatis, religionis ac pietatis exemplo, proli tuae clarissimae, cunctisque mortalibus prae luxisti! Tuis me precibus, o S. Joachim, adjuva, ut et ego gratum Deo domicilium in corde meo prae parem, constantiique pietatis affectu illud exornem. Amen.
blocks.english: O Saint Joachim, to whom a name was given signifying preparation of the Lord, thou wast chosen by God to prepare the living temple of God in which His only-begotten Son was pleased to dwell. O most blessed father, from whom was born that daughter raised to be the Mother of God and Queen of heaven and earth! With what love and reverence thou didst receive her, with what care and solicitude thou didst nourish her! With what splendid example of humility, religion, and devotion thou didst shine before thy most illustrious child and all mortals! Help me with thy prayers, O Saint Joachim, that I too may prepare in my heart a dwelling pleasing to God and adorn it with a steadfast spirit of devotion. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: Checked against the cited 1879 printed edition. The printed reading is “cui recte id nomen est inditum; a quo processit illa filia; O quanto illam amore et reverentia excepisti”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.

blocks.source: Oratio ad S. Matrem Annam.
blocks.english: Prayer to the Holy Mother Anne.

blocks.source: O gratiosa Domina, o benedicta Mater Anna! bene Anna, hoc est gratia, tibi nomen obtigit; quia tibi coelum vivum, omnibus coelis majus, in benedicto utero tuo portare, et in hanc lucem edere a Deo concessum est! O quanta felicitas, quae coelum capere non potuerat, Filia tua immaculato gremio clausa fuit! O coelestis Mater, radix vitae illustris, flos pulcherrimus, fructusque vitae nostrae dulcissimus Christus Jesus ascendit. Laetare, o Anna sterilis! quoniam ex Filia tua Filius natus est nobis, cujus nomen vocatum est magni consilii, hoc est, salutis totius mundi, Angelus. Fac me, o Mater benedicta, gratia, quam ex gratiarum fonte abunde hausisti, participem, ut in amore dilectissimi Nepotis tui Jesu, et protectione dulcissimae Fili ae tuae Mariae vivam et moriar. Amen.
blocks.english: O gracious lady, O blessed Mother Anne! Well did the name Anne, that is grace, fall to thee, for God granted thee to carry in thy blessed womb and bring into this world the living heaven, greater than all the heavens! For Him whom the heavens of heavens could not contain, thy daughter enclosed in her immaculate womb. Thou art, O chosen mother, the root of that rod of Jesse, from which arose the fairest flower and sweetest fruit of our life, Christ Jesus. Rejoice, O barren Anne, for from thy daughter a Son was born to us whose name was called Angel of great counsel, that is, of the salvation of the whole world. Make me, O blessed mother, a sharer in the grace which thou hast drawn abundantly from the fountain of graces, that I may live and die in the love of thy most beloved grandson Jesus and under the protection of thy sweetest daughter Mary. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: Checked against the cited 1879 printed edition. The printed reading is “quem enim coeli coelorum capere non poterant, Filia tua immaculato gremio suo conclusit. Tu es, o electa Mater, radix illa virgae Jesse, ex qua flos pulcherrimus, fructusque vitae nostrae dulcissimus Christus Jesus ascendit”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: O gracious lady, O blessed Mother Anne! Well did the name Anne, that is grace, fall to thee, for God granted thee to carry in thy blessed womb and bring into this world the living heaven, greater than all the heavens! O what happiness: He whom heaven could not contain was enclosed in thy daughter’s immaculate womb! O heavenly mother, illustrious root of life, from whom arose the fairest flower and sweetest fruit of our life, Christ Jesus. Rejoice, O barren Anne, for from thy daughter a Son was born to us whose name was called Angel of great counsel, that is, of the salvation of the whole world. Make me, O blessed mother, a sharer in the grace which thou hast drawn abundantly from the fountain of graces, that I may live and die in the love of thy most beloved grandson Jesus and under the protection of thy sweetest daughter Mary. Amen.

blocks.source: Oratio ad Ambos SS. Joachim et Annam.
blocks.english: Prayer to Both Saints Joachim and Anne.

blocks.source: O castum ac beatum parturturum, Joachim et Anna, vobis omnis creatura obstricta est; per vos enim donum omnium donorum praestantissimum Creatori obtulit, nempe castam matrem, quae sola Creatore digna erat. Vestra dignitas ex meritu cognoscitur, quem Dei perpetuo obsequio prompte consecrastis; coniuro vos, obsecro, junctam huic sacrificio hostiam manibus vestris Deo omnipotenti offerte omnesque hujus in me miseris defectus vestra, quam apud Deum invenistis, gratia compensate.
blocks.english: O chaste and blessed pair of turtledoves, Joachim and Anne, every creature is indebted to you; for through you it offered the Creator the most excellent gift of all gifts, the chaste Mother who alone was worthy of the Creator. Your dignity is known from the immaculate fruit of your womb, whom you readily consecrated to God’s perpetual service. I beseech you, offer my heart, a victim joined to this sacrifice, with your hands to almighty God; and through the grace you have found with God make up all the deficiencies of this gift of mine.
blocks.editorialNote: Checked against the cited 1879 printed edition. The printed reading is “O castum ac beatum par turturum; ex immaculato ventris vestri fructu; cor meum obsecro; hujus mei muneris”. The attached Latin is retained; prepared English follows the documented reading where it differs.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: O chaste and blessed parents, Joachim and Anne, every creature is indebted to you; for through you it offered the Creator the most excellent gift of all gifts, the chaste Mother who alone was worthy of the Creator. Your dignity is known from the merit which you readily consecrated to God’s perpetual service. I implore and beseech you: with your hands offer to almighty God the victim joined to this sacrifice, and through the grace you have found with God make up all its deficiencies in miserable me.
